# LiveForge Agent Context

## What this project is

LiveForge is an MIT-licensed Go 1.26+ live streaming server. It ingests, transmuxes, and delivers audio/video through multiple protocols from one server process. The core is organized as `core/`, protocol and feature modules live under `module/`, reusable media primitives live under `pkg/`, and integration tooling lives under `tools/`.

## Capability matrix

| Capability | Publish | Play | Default port or path | Prerequisites |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTMP | Yes | Yes | 1935 | None beyond the Go build |
| RTSP | Yes | Yes | 8554 plus RTP range | TCP-interleaved and UDP support separate audio/video SETUP tracks; track IDs must be unique and eligible before transport allocation; UDP needs reachable RTP ports |
| SRT | Yes | Yes | 6000 | Optional AES passphrase |
| WebRTC WHIP/WHEP | Yes | Yes | 8443 | SDP offers are limited to 1 MiB; ICE/TURN and secure browser context are required where applicable |
| HLS | No | Yes | 8080, `/{stream}.m3u8` | HTTP stream module |
| LL-HLS | No | Yes | 8080, `/{stream}.m3u8` | `http_stream.llhls.enabled=true` |
| DASH | No | Yes | 8080, `/{stream}.mpd` | HTTP stream module |
| HTTP-FLV | No | Yes | 8080, `/{stream}.flv` | HTTP stream module |
| FMP4 | No | Yes | 8080, `/{stream}.mp4` | HTTP stream module |
| GB28181 | Device ingest and server-initiated playback | Via the shared stream hub | SIP 5060 and RTP 40000-50000 by default | SIP/RTP reachability and device configuration |
| WebSocket-FLV | No | Yes | 8080, `/ws/{stream}.{format}` | `websocket.enabled=true` |

The implementation supports protocol bridging through the shared stream hub. Exact codec compatibility depends on the source, destination, and whether the audio transcoding build is enabled.

Server startup is transactional across registered modules. If a listener or module fails to initialize, shutdown preserves the original error and closes only modules whose initialization was attempted, in reverse order. Later uninitialized modules are not closed, and SRT close remains safe before initialization. Normal RTSP listener closure is not logged as an accept error.

HLS, LL-HLS, and DASH keep the atomic GOP-cache snapshot continuous with subsequent live interframes and only advertise video segments that begin at a keyframe. The initial LL-HLS playlist waits for one completed segment because the bundled Hls.js rejects a part-only initial level, and it omits that completed segment's PART tags so cold startup cannot append the same media twice. Subsequent blocking reloads retain PART tags for the latest completed segment so a client that already consumed those parts correlates the completed segment instead of fetching and appending its full URI again. This avoids the old three-segment wait and segment-boundary `bufferAppendError` while preserving low-latency part consumption. DASH returns its MPD after the first completed keyframe-bounded segment, caps `minimumUpdatePeriod` at two seconds for timely long-GOP discovery, retains exact per-segment durations in `SegmentTimeline`, and configures dash.js with a one-fragment live delay instead of a fixed number of seconds.

The Console has a verified browser workflow for a WHIP source carrying H.265/HEVC video and Opus audio. Its Preview surface covers HTTP-FLV, WS-FLV, HTTP-TS, FMP4, HLS, DASH, WHEP realtime, and WHEP Live. WHIP maps the independent audio/video RTP clocks onto one session timeline using packet-arrival offsets, so a track callback or codec clock cannot introduce a fixed multi-second DTS offset. Incompatible HTTP outputs use a combined transcode reader that starts at the cached GOP source position, preserving target audio history and live source video; cached video is filtered by its video-only DTS range so it is not duplicated. HLS, LL-HLS, and DASH continue from the atomic snapshot cursor without a cross-track DTS watermark, so a later audio DTS cannot hide a valid live video frame. Plain HTTP FMP4 creates a near-zero timeline when its shared muxer starts and preserves relative DTS/PTS across fragments; later subscribers receive shared already-muxed bytes rather than a private timestamp rewrite. The Console uses MSE `segments` mode and starts at the first buffered timestamp so explicit `tfdt` values and signed HEVC B-frame composition offsets remain intact. MSE failure tears down the fetch, reader, queue, SourceBuffer, and object URL; end-of-stream waits for queued appends to drain. WHEP Live uses the atomic source-ring cursor for uninterrupted video and a separate target-codec reader for transcoded audio. Verification requires a decoded frame, non-zero video dimensions, an advancing media clock, and no media error; a `Playing` status string alone is not evidence of playback. WHEP also exposes decoded-frame, FPS, keyframe, loss, and audio RTP statistics. Use [docs/recipes/whip-h265-opus-playback.md](docs/recipes/whip-h265-opus-playback.md).

## Build profiles

The normal build is:

```bash
go build -o bin/liveforge ./cmd/liveforge
```

Audio transcoding is a separate build profile:

```bash
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags audiocodec -o bin/liveforge ./cmd/liveforge
```

The tagged build needs `libavcodec`, `libswresample`, and `libavutil` development libraries. A build without the tag must be described as having audio transcoding disabled, even if FFmpeg is installed on the host.

## Installation and release truth

Source builds are available from the repository. Versioned binaries and the GHCR image are published by the release workflow only when a `v*` tag is pushed and the workflow succeeds. Release binaries use the portable default build and do not include optional audio transcoding; use a source or Docker `audiocodec` build for that capability. Until a release workflow succeeds, do not tell a user to pull an image or download a release asset.

The local Docker Compose workflow builds the image from source by default. A released image can be selected with `LIVEFORGE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/im-pingo/liveforge:vX.Y.Z`, followed by `docker pull` and `docker compose up -d --no-build`; the GHCR package must be public for anonymous pulls, otherwise run `docker login ghcr.io` first.

## Useful HTTP endpoints

- Health: `GET /api/v1/server/health`
- Server information: `GET /api/v1/server/info`
- Server statistics: `GET /api/v1/server/stats`
- Stream list: `GET /api/v1/streams?q=optional-filter`
- Stream detail: `GET /api/v1/streams/{stream_key}`
- Metrics: `GET /metrics` when the metrics module is enabled
- Runtime config status: `GET /api/v1/server/config` (redacted source/version/failure/restart state)
- Runtime config refresh: `POST /api/v1/server/config/refresh` (asynchronous, operator/admin)
- Cluster status: `GET /api/v1/cluster/status`
- SIP Gateway calls: `/api/v1/sipgateway/calls`
- Recordings and DVR: `/api/v1/recordings*`, `/api/v1/dvr/*`
- Security and audit: `GET /api/v1/security/status`, `GET /api/v1/audit`
- WHIP publish: `POST /webrtc/whip/{stream_key}` with an SDP offer of at most 1 MiB
- WHEP play: `POST /webrtc/whep/{stream_key}` with an SDP offer of at most 1 MiB
- GB28181 API: `/api/v1/gb28181/*` when SIP and GB28181 are enabled

The complete HTTP contract is [docs/api/openapi.yaml](docs/api/openapi.yaml). Management responses use a JSON envelope with `code`, `message`, and optional `data`; GB28181 responses are direct JSON and WebRTC uses SDP/plain text.
Management authentication accepts `api.auth.bearer_token`, named viewer/operator/admin tokens, or an authenticated console session. `GET /api/v1/server/health` remains public. TLS API listeners set `Secure` on the HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict `lf_session` cookie; plain HTTP listeners leave it unset for local development. The permission-aware console tabs, in order, are Streams, GB28181, Config, Cluster, SIP Calls, Storage, and Security. Recent Audit is a surface inside Security, not a separate tab. Viewer reads status, operator controls calls/refresh/kick/live-playback, and admin owns deletions/debug/internal mutation.

Recording supports FLV, FMP4, MP4, TS, and HLS plus authenticated listing, status, metadata, range download, inline range playback, and deletion. `GET /api/v1/recordings/{recordingPath}/play` returns the completed media with a format-specific MIME type, `Content-Disposition: inline`, and standard HTTP Range behavior; active/not-ready recordings return 409. DVR exposes session and storage status and serves time-shift playlists/segments on its configured listener. The Storage Console previews completed recordings (native MP4/fMP4 or mpegts.js FLV/TS) and opens HLS playback for DVR sessions with segments. The DVR listener permits non-credentialed cross-origin HLS fetches for this split-port Console, while playlist and segment GETs still run synchronous subscribe authorization hooks only and do not emit asynchronous subscribe lifecycle work. Recording preview reuses the authenticated management session; the Console never persists or appends bearer tokens, so configure DVR subscribe authorization for the independent media listener. Use [docs/recipes/recording-dvr-management.md](docs/recipes/recording-dvr-management.md).

RTP/GB28181 cluster signaling paths are configurable. Node clients load current atomic credentials for every request, preferring `api.auth.bearer_token`, then the first named admin token. Rotation is hot; when auth is configured without an admin credential, the request fails locally. Peer error bodies are bounded and redacted. Use [docs/recipes/cluster-relay-operations.md](docs/recipes/cluster-relay-operations.md).

## Runtime configuration

The bootstrap YAML file is read once during startup. The `config/runtime` manager then polls the selected source (`file`, `http`, `https`, `consul`, or `redis`) in a background goroutine. It parses, normalizes, validates, hashes, and atomically publishes immutable snapshots. Runtime reads are one atomic pointer load and do not perform file/network I/O, wait on channels, or contend with refresh locks.

For HTTP sources, `runtime.source: http` requires an `http://` URL and `runtime.source: https` requires an `https://` URL. Redirects are disabled, including same-origin redirects. `ETag` and `Last-Modified` conditional validators come only from the last accepted snapshot, so malformed, invalid, or unapplied responses cannot advance them. `X-Config-Version` remains source version metadata and is not treated as an ETag.

`SIGHUP` and `POST /api/v1/server/config/refresh` only schedule asynchronous refresh. A source timeout, backend failure, malformed document, or validation error keeps the last valid snapshot active and updates manager status. Hot policy changes can be delivered to reloadable modules; listener addresses, module enablement, TLS files/mode, port ranges, and audio codec enablement are classified as `restart_required`. Status and Prometheus expose accepted/rejected/application-failed changes, callback failures, superseded callbacks, and pending restart paths. Simulcast configuration remains deferred because no layer selection runtime exists.

Documented non-positive scalar sentinels retain their owning module defaults: SIP Gateway calls use 100, cluster eviction uses 3 failures, audit retains 1000 entries, and HTTP/Consul sources cap documents at 4 MiB. Explicit empty RTSP, WebRTC, and GB28181 port ranges are valid and select their module fallback behavior; non-empty ranges require two ordered positive ports. Exact semantics are annotated in `docs/config/config.schema.json`.

Runnable source examples are in [docs/recipes/runtime-config-sources.md](docs/recipes/runtime-config-sources.md). The deprecated `auth.api.bearer_token` migrates only when `api.auth.bearer_token` is empty; the current path wins if both exist. Credentials must come from environment expansion or an external secret store and are never logged.

## Verification

The documentation contract is checked with:

```bash
tools/check-agent-docs_test.sh
```

The quick package check and complete CI build/test are:

```bash
go test ./...
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags audiocodec ./cmd/liveforge
CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags audiocodec -race -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./...
```

The first command skips FFmpeg-tagged transcoding integration tests. The tagged commands are the complete verification path and require Go 1.26 plus FFmpeg development libraries.

The `lf-test` tool emits human-readable or JSON reports and uses exit code 0 for success, 1 for assertion failure, and 2 for an execution error.

GitHub Actions maintenance uses Node 24-compatible action majors: checkout and setup-go v7, upload-artifact v7, Docker setup-buildx v4, login v4, build-push v7, golangci-lint v9, and action-gh-release v3. Do not reintroduce deprecated Node 20 action versions or the `ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION` workaround.

## Security boundaries

`configs/liveforge.yaml` is a local-development sample. It disables authentication and TLS and uses `admin/admin` for the console. A production deployment must change credentials, enable TLS, enable API and stream authentication, limit exposed ports, configure ICE/TURN correctly, and enable rate limiting where appropriate.

Use [docs/recipes/auth-and-tls.md](docs/recipes/auth-and-tls.md) for transport/auth setup, [docs/recipes/rbac-audit.md](docs/recipes/rbac-audit.md) for the permission matrix and audit recovery, [docs/recipes/sipgateway-management.md](docs/recipes/sipgateway-management.md) for call operations, and [docs/recipes/release-verification.md](docs/recipes/release-verification.md) before claiming an image or binary is available.

## Agent change rule

Every source change must review and update the relevant AI-facing files in the same change. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the mandatory synchronization matrix and review checklist.
